## Finding
The active Branch Garden Report workflow contradicts the filed Arborscaping record for history-rewrite branches. The May 17 completion report and May 25 census say a missing merge base is diagnostic and ahead/behind metrics become misleading. The reporter currently computes those metrics anyway, allowing a structurally foreign branch to be described as merely stale or far behind.

## Change
- Check for a merge base before calculating branch distance.
- Route no-merge-base branches to explicit SALVAGE review before any PRUNE decision.
- Add a regression test proving a preserved foreign-history branch cannot acquire distance-derived stale/prune claims.

## Scope
This changes reporting only. It does not delete branches, merge PRs, alter permissions, or modify the staged version-transition governance proposal in PR #374.

## Evidence
- !/ARBORSCAPE-COMPLETION-REPORT-2026-05-17.md: missing merge base is diagnostic, not cosmetic.
- !-ARBORSCAPING-REPORT-2026-05-25.md: branch distance classification is misleading for orphan histories; salvage precedes pruning.

## Verification
- py -3.13 -B -m unittest tests.test_branch_garden_report tests.test_issue_reconciler -v -> 4 passed.
- uff check .github/scripts/branch_garden_report.py tests/test_branch_garden_report.py -> passed.
- Staged secret-pattern guard and cached diff check -> passed.
title: Fix: preserve foreign branches in garden reports

## Finding
This is not a persistent-writer diagnosis. Logan-directed tasks have been followed by isolated version edits that cross compatibility boundaries without a durable record. Evidence: PR #359 partially changed the OpenTelemetry set and failed resolution; PR #363 changed click across the crewai constraint; PR #364 changed mcp across the crewai constraint. Commits 3cf73fab, 0eab6bdf, bc19e3f1, and d0fb10d5 also show unrecorded runtime or lock churn on May 25-26, 2026.

## Change
- Stage VERSION-TRANSITIONS.md as a compatibility and rationale ledger.
- Require a same-PR ledger row for agent-authored changes or reverts to governed runtime, dependency, workflow action, or registry versions.
- Permit only authenticated Dependabot requirements.txt-only PRs as a PR-audited exception, still blocked by required dependency resolution.
- Add the check-version-transitions PR validator, protect the ledger from deletion and Dependabot auto-merge, and make the Dependabot gate await the new check after activation.

## Activation
This PR is draft and risk-high because it changes AGENTS and governance surfaces. If Logan approves and it is merged, add check-version-transitions to the active strict required status checks in ruleset 16864823. Until then, the existing Dependabot gate on main remains unchanged.

## Verification
- Focused security and governance tests: 43 passed.
- Ruff check on changed Python surfaces: passed.
- Staged secret-pattern guard and cached diff check: passed.
- Commit-range version-transition guard: passed.
title: Security: require recorded version transitions

Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.7.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project after a sharp decline in financial support. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Addressed high-severity security issues. Impact was limited to specific use cases detailed in the accompanying advisories; overall user exposure was estimated to be marginal.

  • Decompression-bomb safeguards of the streaming API were bypassed:

    1. When HTTPResponse.drain_conn() was called after the response had been read and decompressed partially. (Reported by @​Cycloctane)
    2. During the second HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) or HTTPResponse.stream(amt=N) call when the response was decompressed using the official Brotli library. (Reported by @​kimkou2024)

    See GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j for details.

  • HTTP pools created using ProxyManager.connection_from_url did not strip sensitive headers specified in Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect when redirecting to a different host. (GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc reported by @​christos-spearbit)

Deprecations and Removals

  • Used FutureWarning instead of DeprecationWarning for better visibility of existing deprecation notices. Rescheduled the removal of deprecated features to version 3.0. (urllib3/urllib3#3763)
  • Removed support for end-of-life Python 3.9. (urllib3/urllib3#3720)
  • Removed support for end-of-life PyPy3.10. (urllib3/urllib3#4979)
  • Bumped the minimum supported pyOpenSSL version to 19.0.0. (urllib3/urllib3#3777)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed a bug where HTTPResponse.read(amt=None) was ignoring decompressed data buffered from previous partial reads. (urllib3/urllib3#3636)

v0.25.0

This release deliberately contains backwards-incompatible changes. To avoid automatically picking up releases like this, you should either be pinning the exact version of esbuild in your package.json file (recommended) or be using a version range syntax that only accepts patch upgrades such as ^0.24.0 or ~0.24.0. See npm's documentation about semver for more information.

  • Restrict access to esbuild's development server (GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99)

    This change addresses esbuild's first security vulnerability report. Previously esbuild set the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to * to allow esbuild's development server to be flexible in how it's used for development. However, this allows the websites you visit to make HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server, which gives read-only access to your source code if the website were to fetch your source code's specific URL. You can read more information in the report.

    Starting with this release, CORS will now be disabled, and requests will now be denied if the host does not match the one provided to --serve=. The default host is 0.0.0.0, which refers to all of the IP addresses that represent the local machine (e.g. both 127.0.0.1 and 192.168.0.1). If you want to customize anything about esbuild's development server, you can put a proxy in front of esbuild and modify the incoming and/or outgoing requests.

    In addition, the serve() API call has been changed to return an array of hosts instead of a single host string. This makes it possible to determine all of the hosts that esbuild's development server will accept.

This release delivers prototype-pollution hardening for the Node HTTP adapter, adds an opt-in allowedSocketPaths allowlist to mitigate SSRF via Unix domain sockets, fixes a keep-alive socket memory leak, and ships supply-chain hardening across CI and security docs.
